title: Magnetic Resonance Imaging of the Head and Neck
cms_cov_policy:
<p>Title XVIII of the Social Security Act, &#167;1862(a)(1)(A) allows coverage and payment for only those services that are considered to be reasonable and necessary for the diagnosis or treatment of illness or injury or to improve the functioning of a malformed body member.</p>
<p>CMS Internet-Only Manual, Pub. 100-03, Medicare National Coverage Determinations (NCD) Manual, Chapter 1, Part 4, &#167;220.2 Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI)</p>
keywords: Magnetic Resonance Imaging|MRI|Orbit, Face, and/or Neck|MRI of Head and Neck
associated_info: <p><strong>Documentation Requirements</strong><br /><br />Documentation supporting the medical necessity should be legible, maintained in the patient&rsquo;s medical record, and must be made available to the A/B MAC upon request.<br /><br /><strong>Utilization Guidelines</strong><br /><br />In general, it is not medically necessary to perform myelography, CT examinations, and MRI examinations for evaluation of the same condition on the same day. The medical record should document the necessity for evaluations in addition to an MRI scan. <br /><br />It is expected that these services would be performed as indicated by current medical literature and/or standards of practice. When services are performed in excess of established parameters, they may be subject to review for medical necessity.</p>
issue: <p><span style="line-height: 107%; background: white;">This LCD outlines limited coverage for this service with specific details under <em><strong>Coverage Indications, Limitations and/or Medical Necessity</strong></em>.</span></p>
issue_change: <p>No changes between Proposed LCD and Final LCD.</p>
